findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee begin to don gloves without handwashing. CORRECTED- the employee was interrupted and directed to wash hands. The employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet. Inspector provided education and demonstrated correct hand washing, which the employee modeled afterwards (rinse hands, scrub with soap, dry with paper towel and use barrier to turn off to avoid recontaminating hands). Review hand washing procedures and times to wash with all employees who serve or handle food. Inspector provided a handout regarding times to wash hands. Times to wash hands include but are not limited to: before donning gloves, after using using the restroom, between working with raw and ready to eat foods, etc.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw chicken stored over ready to eat (RTE) cooked and peeled eggs in the standing cooler. CORRECTED- chicken was moved below the eggs. Ensure all animals proteins are stored to reflect increasing internal cooking temperatures (top-> bottom= RTE foods, unwashed produce, washed produce, raw eggs/ shellfish/ seafood, pork, and chicken) to prevent the cross contamination of foods. Inspector provided a handout to the PIC.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.[P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the triple sink to be set up in the following format: wash-sanitize-rinse. CORRECTED- the sink was remade to reflect proper ware washing: (wash- rinse-sanitize), and a handout was provided to the PIC. Rinsing after sanitizing prevents proper contact time between the sanitizer and food contact surface. Ensure the triple sink is always made to reflect proper ware washing moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(A) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (A) Hot water manual operations by immersion for at least 30 seconds and as specified under § 4-501.111.[P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cooked rice holding an internal temperature of 114F. CORRECTED- the item was moved under TIME AS CONTROL (TAC)- the item was stated to have been prepared at 11 AM, and will be used or discarded by 3PM. Once rice (or noodles, or vegetables) are cooked they become temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods- and therefore must be held below 41F or above 135F to prevent the growth of pathogens. Ensure all TCS foods are kept outside of the temperature danger zone.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple sauces labeled “refrigerate after opening” held on the counter. Sauces included garlic Parmesan and garlic buffalo sauce. CORRECTED- The PIC stated the bottles were just opened and items were moved to cold holding. Ensure all TCS foods are cold held below 41F or hot held above 135F to prevent the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The steam table in the kitchen- that is the only piece of equipment that is used for hot holding was observed to not be functioning. The PIC stated that there is an electrical issue with the outlets that is causing issues with the equipment. Disposable votive burners that are typically used for short-term hot holding are being used under foil pans. These burners are allowing the food items hot holding to maintain temperatures of 135F and above for the time being. This is not a long term solution and the steam table either needs to be repaired or another method of hot holding needs to be obtained. A follow up is scheduled for 5/20/2026 to ensure the steam table is functional or another method of hot holding has been obtained.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw fish in reduced oxygen packaging thawing in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- education was provided regarding thawing in reduced oxygen packaging, and packages were cut to be vented. Ensure items in reduced oxygen packaging are vented or removed from packaging when thawing to prevent the growth of anaerobic bacteria such as Clostridium botulinum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed plates being stored at the server station with the food contact surface facing upwards, and silverware stored with the food contact surface outwards. CORRECTED- the plates were flipped and the silverware was inverted. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored in a manner that protects against bare hand contamination and contamination from the environment.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The PIC stated they no longer had sanitizing test strips since the dish machine was removed. The facility uses bleach for chemical sanitation at the triple sink, and quaternary ammonia for sanitizer in the bottle used for food contact surfaces. The inspector will return for a follow up inspection on 5/20/26 to ensure test strips have been obtained. Ensure a test kit (for BOTH chlorine bleach and quaternary ammonia) is available to verify proper sanitizing concentrations of chemicals used to sanitize food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed used water in the basin of a mop bucket in the back of the kitchen. CORRECTED- the mop water was dumped. Mops absorb fats, oils, and grease. Ensure mop water (once used- classified as waste water) is dumped immediately after use moving forward.
* This violation was previously noted as violation #55
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. [P]
